newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks close with drop of 2.24 percent.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks close with drop of 2.24 percent.

text.p: Swiss shares ended sharply lower on Friday with the blue-chip SMI losing 2.24 percent.
Traders said prices were hit by derivative-related selling linked to the day's Soffex option expiry as well as by profit-taking, stop-loss orders and a weaker start on Wall Street.
"After the recent string of high closings, a consolidation is welcomed as fundamentals are unchanged," one dealer said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) dropped 2.24 percent or 131.2 points at 5,737.1 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 1.85 percent or 68.68 points at 3,636.27.
Dealers said they expected the SMI to move next week in a range between 5,750 and 6,000 points.
Shares of volume leader Novartis, which is expected to announce sales figures for the first half of 1997 on July 24, dropped 70 francs to 2.350.
Most dealers said they expected good to very good Novartis results. "But there was probably still some profit-taking going on", one dealer said about the falling price.
Pharma giant Roche, which announced its sales figures on Tuesday, fell 305 francs to 14,310. The drop was mainly due to derivitives trading, dealers said.
Financial shares were also under pressure.
Credit Suisse Group lost four percent or eight francs to 197.50. SBC dropped two percent or 10.5 francs to 403. UBS closed 34 francs lower at 1,665.
Insurers Zurich, Winterthur and Swiss Re were also lower.
Zurich dropped 12 francs to 583. Winterthur, which was sought on a speculative basis since last week, came down 43 francs to close at 1,417. Swiss Re was 48 francs lower at 2,108.
